column36: The Jacksonville Jaguars have basically built a second home across the pond, but why London?, It all started with owner Shahid Khan. Khan bought the Jaguars in 2011, and just one year later,, Jacksonville became the first, and still only, NFL team to commit to multiple seasons of London, games. Khan, who was born in Pakistan, had always felt a connection to the UK, and he saw London as, a great way to grow the Jaguars brand. So when the Rams pulled out of an agreement to play games, across multiple seasons in London, Khan stepped in. He offered the Jags to fill in on a four-year, agreement beginning in 2013 that would have the team play a home game per year in London for four, years. In 2013, Khan also bought Premier League club Fulham FC, giving him a major foothold in the UK, sports market. That year, Jacksonville played its first game across the pond versus the 49ers at, Wembley Stadium, and they haven't looked back, playing in London every single year since 2013,, except for 2020. They now have 14 London appearances, the most out of any NFL team,, and a 7-7 record across the pond. The Jaguars have since renewed their London commitment twice,, and as of 2025, they're contracted to play six games there over three seasons, including two, back-to-back this season. The team also specifically runs its Wembley Stadium operations, independently, meaning they keep all their ticket and seating revenue, food, beverage, and merchandise, sales, and get to set ticket prices. What started as a four-year experiment has become part of the, Jaguars' identity. Jacksonville doesn't just play in London, London is part of the Jaguars. column36: Over a decade ago, the NFL set a mission to bring football to the UK, and they contributed over $13 million to build their house, which is now known as Tottenham Hotspur Stadium., Here's how we got here. Back in 2007, the NFL played its first regular season game in London at Wembley Stadium., Eight years later, the NFL and Tottenham Hotspur made a much bigger commitment., In 2015, they signed a 10-year partnership calling for a minimum of two NFL games per year to be played at Tottenham's new stadium., And this wasn't just any stadium., When Tottenham Hotspur Stadium opened in 2019, it was designed specifically to host soccer and NFL games, with dedicated NFL locker rooms and media facilities., It was even built with a retractable soccer pitch that uncovers a permanent underground artificial turf field built directly to NFL specifications., Then in 2023, the partnership got even bigger., Tottenham was officially named the home of the NFL in the UK as a part of the agreement that included an extension through the 2029-2030 season., And since opening, Tottenham has hosted NFL games every year, except in 2020 due to COVID., Keating off the 2026-27 season, at Tottenham Stadium this Sunday will be the Indianapolis Colts vs. the Washington Commanders., Now, this isn't the farthest trip teams will have to make for an international game by any means this season., The Commanders are just 3,733 miles from Tottenham, and the Colts have just over a 4,000-mile trip to make., However, this is the Colts and Commanders' first time playing in this stadium., Both teams did play at Wembley Stadium in 2016, but the time change, weather, and other factors will still have major implications in this game., One thing we do know is that Tottenham has become a key part of the NFL's international strategy., Is this a stadium you would want to check out?, Let us know in the comments below.
